name: AWS + Cloud
sub: S3, EMR, CloudWatch, Grafana, orchestration - 14 days
desc: The cloud infrastructure and observability layer for your data pipeline. Goes deep on CloudWatch and Grafana -- the exact AWS-native monitoring stack the JD's near-real-time dashboard implies -- plus serverless orchestration, Glue/Athena, and cost control.
tip: The most expensive AWS mistake is forgetting to terminate a cluster -- set a $20 budget alert immediately. For Grafana specifically, the strongest interview answer isn't 'I built a dashboard' but 'I provisioned it as Terraform-managed JSON so it reproduces across environments and survives a workspace rebuild.'

r: IAM least privilege
Grant only permissions actually needed. Never AdministratorAccess for an app.
S3 bucket naming
Globally unique. Cannot change once created. Plan carefully.
Core vs Task nodes
Core = compute + HDFS storage. Task = compute only. Spot on task nodes.
TERMINATE the cluster
EMR runs 24/7 until stopped. Terminate immediately after the job finishes.
VPC endpoint for S3
Free private route from EMR to S3. Saves NAT gateway costs per GB.
EMR vs Glue
EMR = managed cluster you control. Glue = serverless ETL for simple jobs.
S3 lifecycle rules
Auto-move old data to cheaper tiers. Prevents unbounded S3 costs.
Shared responsibility
AWS secures infrastructure. YOU secure IAM, encryption, bucket access.
CloudWatch namespace
Container for related metrics, e.g. AWS/EMR, AWS/S3, or a custom Pipeline/ namespace.
Amazon Managed Grafana IAM
The WORKSPACE needs an IAM role to read CloudWatch -- not your personal credentials.
Grafana multi-dim alerting
One rule definition can fire many alert instances -- one per label combination, e.g. per source.
Athena cost lever
$5 per TB scanned. Partition pruning (filter on the partition column) is the #1 cost control.
